matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can become an X (two crossing diagonals) and vice‑versa by moving a single diagonal stick within the same character, changing its value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V or X and the numeric discrepancy suggests a five‑unit adjustment.
matchstick.example: Changing X in XIII to V yields VIII, reducing the value by five.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides; the difference tells how much the total must be increased or decreased.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the Roman numerals, before deciding which stick to move.
matchstick.example: 12 = 17 gives a discrepancy of 5, indicating a ±5 change is needed.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign consists of two horizontal sticks; after moving a stick it must still represent a valid equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from any part of the equation, ensure it is not taken from the equality sign unless another stick is added to keep it as '='.
matchstick.example: Do not remove a horizontal bar from '=', because it would become a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each affected symbol must still be a recognized Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a legal operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Turning X into V yields a valid numeral; turning I into a single diagonal would be invalid.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a diagonal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure its orientation matches the target shape's required orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal stick cannot be used to create an I, which requires a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator is allowed only if the new shape corresponds to a legal operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from or to an operator, verify that the resulting symbol is a valid operator.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is valid; moving a diagonal would create an illegal shape.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to check equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each proposed move, before finalizing the solution.
matchstick.example: After turning X to V, recompute 8 + 4 = 12 to confirm the equation holds.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns '+' into '-', and the removed stick can be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests a subtraction instead of addition and a vertical stick is available for relocation.
matchstick.example: XII = XIII + IV → XII = XIII - IV by moving the vertical from '+'.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be taken from one character (decreasing its value) and attached to another (increasing its value) to balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy cannot be fixed by a single‑character change, consider moving a stick between two numerals.
matchstick.example: Take a diagonal from a V (5) to turn it into I (1) and add it to another V, turning that V into X (10), thereby shifting 5 units.

matchstick.title: Discrepancy‑5 heuristic for X↔V adjustment
matchstick.principle: If the computed difference between sides is exactly 5 (or –5) and the equation contains an X or V, try converting an X to V (or V to X) to adjust the value by five.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, if it equals five and an X or V is present, apply the V↔X transformation.
matchstick.example: 12 = 17 (difference 5) → change the X in XIII to V, giving VIII and balancing the equation.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model abstracts away from the physical sticks and treats symbol parts as interchangeable, forgetting that a diagonal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick being moved; only place it where the same orientation is required.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think any stick can be taken from any symbol, including the '=' sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the equality sign as immutable; never relocate its sticks unless you also replace them to keep it as '='.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets to validate the source character after a stick is removed, resulting in shapes that are not Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that both the source and destination symbols are still valid characters.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric effect and ignores whether the resulting operator is allowed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving sticks from or to an operator, ensure the resulting shape matches one of '+', '-', '='.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model jumps to random transformations without first understanding how far the equation is from being correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Start by calculating the Arabic values of both sides and the discrepancy; use this metric to guide which stick to move.
